title: add deterministic-intake-checksum-and-changelog-orchestrator
author: Priya Menon
description:
Context and motivation: onboarding artifacts (manifests, performance profiles, and provenance blobs) were arriving with non-deterministic ordering and no compact fingerprint, which made incremental changelog synthesis noisy and caused duplicate release fragments. This PR introduces a deterministic intake checksum (content-addressed, order-insensitive fingerprint) plus a Changelog Orchestrator service that consumes intake events and composes compact release deltas for the model registry and the releases pipeline.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds intake/checksum: a deterministic, canonical hashing step for uploads that normalizes artifact lists and ignores metadata fields marked as 'volatile' (upload timestamps, ephemeral tags). The checksum is stable across semantically identical payloads.
- Introduces changelog-orchestrator: a small service that subscribes to intake events, groups related artifacts into micro-deltas, computes a concise human-facing changelog entry (title, short bullet summary, perf delta tags), and emits a signed release fragment to the release-assembler pipeline.
- Adds heuristics to merge performance-profile diffs: when quantization/latency changes are present we summarize both median-latency and 95th-percentile regressions and attach tags (perf:regression/perf:improvement) if thresholds are crossed.
- Provides a backfill job to re-hash historical manifests (best-effort) and retroactively assemble missing release fragments to reduce churn for existing models.

Checklist:
- [x] deterministic checksum implementation (canonicalize + multihash)
- [x] intake webhook patch to compute and store checksum on manifest records
- [x] changelog-orchestrator consumer and emitter with unit tests
- [x] performance-delta summarizer with threshold config and sample-based confidence bounds
- [x] CLI hook (registry-cli changelog preview) for maintainers to preview the assembled fragment before publish
- [x] backfill job + migration script (non-blocking)
- [x] integration tests for event flow and signed fragment verification

Commits (summary):
- feat(checksum): canonical serializer and multihash helper (Priya)
- feat(intake): attach checksum to manifest.upsert and event payload (Priya)
- feat(orchestrator): new service scaffold + consumer loop + signer (Priya)
- feat(perf): perf-delta summarizer and threshold configs (Omar)
- chore(cli): changelog preview command and output formatter (Marta)
- test: integration tests for end-to-end flow (CI)
- chore(migrations): backfill migration and README for operators

Files changed (high level):
- services/intake/src/checksum.ts (new) - canonicalize + hash logic
- services/intake/src/manifest-handler.ts - attach checksum to DB model and event payload
- services/changelog-orchestrator/* (new) - consumer, summarizer, signer, http webhook emitter
- registry-cli/src/preview-changelog.ts - preview command (new)
- migrations/202602-backfill-checksum.js - backfill migration script
- tests/integration/changelog-flow.test.ts - end-to-end test (new)

Testing and CI: initial runs flagged a flaky test in perf summarizer (95th percentile estimator under small-sample edge cases). Reworked estimator to use bootstrapped CIs; CI now passes all unit and integration suites. Lint and typecheck green. Load test (smoke) for orchestrator consumer shows ~1200 events/min on a single t3.large-equivalent worker; will scale with consumer groups.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: 1) make checksum opt-in for private deployments via config flag (so on-prem customers can skip if they have a different provenance system), 2) confirm signer key rotation path."
- Priya (author): "Added 'registry.features.checksum.enabled' toggle and documented it. Signer rotates via kms:rotate endpoint; added rotate test and ops README section."
- Marta Kline (review): "CLI preview UX is good. Suggest including perf percentiles in the preview table and a --raw flag to output structured fragment for copy/paste."
- Priya: "Added percentiles and --raw JSON output. Kept default as concise text for maintainers."
- Omar Hassan (review): "Perf summarizer: switch threshold config to percent-based bands instead of absolute ms for model-size-agnostic behavior."
- Priya: "Switched to percent thresholds and added migration note for older numeric thresholds. Kept backwards compatibility (legacy thresholds converted at read-time)."

Operational notes:
- Feature toggle: registry.features.checksum.enabled (default: true for hosted; false for private-installer unless explicitly enabled)
- Backfill: non-blocking job that runs in background; operators can run migrations/202602-backfill-checksum.js to speed catch-up.
- Observability: new metrics exported by orchestrator: changelog.fragments.emitted, changelog.merge.conflicts, perf.delta.alerts, checksum.collisions (expected 0). Traces added for event-to-fragment path.

Security and signing: fragments are signed with registry-release-key v1 (KMS-backed). The orchestrator verifies signature before emitting to release-assembler; assembler continues to assert valid signature. Added unit tests for signature verification and a short playbook for key rotation in the ops README.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- No user-visible breaking changes to the API contract. Manifest records gain a new optional checksum field. The changelog-orchestrator only starts producing fragments when checksum is present or when orchestrator is configured to accept older artifacts.
- Migration is best-effort: backfill will annotate older manifests but does not rewrite user-submitted manifests; release-assembler deduplicates fragments by checksum to avoid double entries.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature toggle (this PR)
2) Enable for hosted registry and run backfill during a low-traffic window
3) Monitor metrics (perf.delta.alerts and changelog.fragments.emitted) and errors for 72h
4) Gradually flip toggle for private-installer customers who opt-in

Notes for maintainers: the orchestrator is purposely lightweight; it is horizontally scalable via consumer group instances and keeps only recent fragment state in Redis. Full fragment history is persisted in releases store. See services/changelog-orchestrator/README.md for developer notes and local run instructions.

release_notes: Adds deterministic intake checksum for manifest deduplication and a Changelog Orchestrator that composes compact, signed release fragments with perf-delta summaries. Includes a CLI preview, backfill migration, and feature toggle for opt-in behavior on private installs.
